task: Quality Control Plane semantic execution: resolve Git-proven deleted legacy routes through durable Product Owner forbidden-route authority without restoring deleted routes as canonical domain ownership.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: PR #673 made Git D changes first-class semantic tombstones and removed DEV_PLAN_SEMANTIC_MUST_EDIT_OUTSIDE_ROUTE from PR #666. Exact-head replay then exposed a narrower gap: the deleted legacy route src/app/szallitas-es-fizetes/page.tsx has intentionally no current canonical domain path, so Plan Before Code reports ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED even though an active durable Product Owner instruction explicitly forbids /szallitas-es-fizetes and the deletion is proven by Git D. Restoring the legacy path to DOMAIN-STOREFRONT would falsely make a forbidden route canonical.
observableOutcomes: An active PO instruction forbidden static route is mapped to its legacy route file when that exact file is present in Git-proven tombstones.
That instruction-governed tombstone is included in INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED with explicit tombstone provenance.

Plan architecture resolution accepts only those deleted paths that are both Git-proven tombstones and instruction-required forbidden routes, without assigning them fake current canonical domain ownership.
An arbitrary deleted unowned path without active forbidden-route authority remains ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED.
unresolvedRisks: A broad deletion exception could hide genuinely unowned architecture changes.
Mapping every forbidden string to a route file could misinterpret non-route forbidden states.
A stale PO instruction could incorrectly preserve legacy route authority after the instruction is retired.

in: Existing PO instruction required-change derivation in Semantic Execution Intelligence.
Existing Plan Before Code architecture unresolved check for Git-proven tombstones.
Regression reproducing deleted /szallitas-es-fizetes under the active shipping/payment instruction.
out: New gate, new instruction registry, or generic deleted-file exception.
Changes to durable PO instruction content or lifecycle.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a fail-closed architecture-boundary defect discovered by replaying a real PO-required route deletion. The highest practical correction is to derive deleted forbidden static-route files from the existing durable instruction authority, bind them to Git tombstone evidence, and adversarially prove that arbitrary unowned deletions remain blocked.

acceptanceCriteria: For PO-INSTRUCTION-SHIPPING-PAYMENT-SEPARATE and a Git tombstone src/app/szallitas-es-fizetes/page.tsx, buildExecutionRoute reports that file in INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED and identifies it as an instruction-governed tombstone.
Plan Before Code does not report ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED for that exact instruction-governed tombstone.
The same path without Git D evidence is not granted tombstone resolution.
A Git D path with no matching active forbidden route remains unresolved when it has no canonical domain.
No legacy /szallitas-es-fizetes path is added to DOMAIN-STOREFRONT canonicalPaths.
invariants: Git D evidence is mandatory for legacy tombstone resolution.
The matching PO instruction must be active and must contain a static forbidden route mapping to the exact tombstone file.
Live files still require normal canonical domain ownership.
Instruction-governed tombstones do not become canonical domain paths.
Retiring or changing the PO instruction removes this resolution authority automatically.

failureModes: A correct PO-required deletion stays blocked because canonical domain ownership intentionally disappears with the legacy route.
A generic tombstone exemption allows arbitrary unowned deleted files through architecture validation.
The instruction route is recognized only while the forbidden file exists, losing authority immediately after successful deletion.
edgeCases: Deleted forbidden static route with active instruction.
Same forbidden route path absent but not Git-deleted in the current transaction.
Deleted unowned path unrelated to any instruction.
Dynamic or wildcard forbidden route that cannot map safely to one static file.
Inactive PO instruction containing an old forbidden route.

alternatives.summary: Derive forbidden static-route tombstones from the existing active PO instruction and require exact Git D evidence before architecture resolution.
alternatives.reason: Preserves fail-closed architecture semantics without making a forbidden legacy route canonical again.
Would declare the explicitly forbidden legacy route canonical after its removal.

alternatives.summary: Skip architecture unresolved checks for every Git D path.
alternatives.reason: Would create a broad deletion bypass for genuinely unowned architecture changes.

specialistReviews.finding: The legacy route should not regain canonical domain ownership merely so a deletion can be validated.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use active instruction authority plus Git D provenance as a tombstone-only architecture resolution.

specialistReviews.finding: Skipping domain checks for all deletions would weaken architecture coverage.
specialistReviews.resolution: Resolution is limited to exact static forbidden-route files derived from active instructions and intersected with Git tombstones.

specialistReviews.finding: The existing execution route already carries tombstones and PO instructions; no parallel registry is required.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend INSTRUCTION_REQUIREMENTS with forbiddenRouteTombstones and consume that evidence in the existing Plan gate.

specialistReviews.finding: The durable instruction is the semantic reason the old combined route must disappear, but it must not become a general architecture owner.
specialistReviews.resolution: Expose instruction-governed tombstone provenance only for exact active forbidden static routes plus Git D evidence.

challenge.scenario: PR #666 deletes /szallitas-es-fizetes and no current Atlas node/domain remains.
challenge.finding: Plan emits ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED despite the deletion being the exact required product decision.
challenge.resolution: Map the active instruction's forbidden static route to its route file and retain it only when that file is a Git-proven tombstone.

challenge.scenario: An unrelated deleted file has no domain.
challenge.finding: It must not benefit from the legacy-route rule.
challenge.resolution: No matching active forbidden route means no instruction tombstone provenance; unresolved remains blocking.

challenge.scenario: The forbidden path is merely absent from the current Atlas but was not deleted in this transaction.
challenge.finding: Absence is not proof of implementation.
challenge.resolution: Require membership in the passed tombstones set before adding forbiddenRouteTombstones.
buildExecutionRoute already filters instructions by lifecycle==='active'; preserve that condition.

challenge.scenario: Forbidden state is display-label or route-key rather than route.
challenge.finding: It cannot safely identify a static filesystem route.
challenge.resolution: Only forbiddenStates with kind route and a staticRouteFile mapping participate.

challenge.scenario: A matching forbidden route exists in an active instruction but the tombstone path belongs to a different static route.
challenge.finding: Instruction presence alone cannot authorize a different deleted path.
challenge.resolution: Intersect the static forbidden-route file with the exact Git tombstones set; no fuzzy or prefix match.

challenge.scenario: A live file matches a forbidden route but is not deleted.
challenge.finding: Legacy tombstone architecture resolution must not convert a surviving forbidden file into an accepted architecture state.
challenge.resolution: forbiddenRouteTombstones is restricted to Git D paths; live forbidden files remain handled by existing forbidden-state enforcement.

challenge.scenario: A forbidden dynamic route such as /termek/:slug cannot map to one stable page file with staticRouteFile.
challenge.finding: Treating dynamic routes as static tombstones could authorize the wrong filesystem target.
challenge.resolution: staticRouteFile already rejects dynamic/wildcard route syntax; preserve fail-closed behavior.

proofPlan: Run plan-only canonical Plan Before Code before implementation.
Unit-test buildExecutionRoute with an active forbidden static route plus matching tombstone and assert INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED plus explicit forbiddenRouteTombstones evidence.
Repeat without tombstone evidence and with an unrelated tombstone; neither may receive instruction-tombstone resolution.
Run exact-head full Quality, TypeScript, Production Build and Completion Truth.
Merge only after lifecycle CLOSE→LEARN exact-head closure passes; then replay PR #666 without changing its product intent.

Bind REQ-TOMBSTONE-ARCHITECTURE-RESOLUTION explicitly to exact-head GUARD-PLAN-BEFORE-CODE authority evidence plus Quality regression proof; Truth Gate must reject any authority claim not covered by producer semantics.

requirements.requirement: Active PO forbidden static routes produce instruction-required tombstone provenance only when exact Git D evidence exists.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unrelated or non-Git-deleted paths may not receive instruction tombstone resolution.

requirements.requirement: Plan Before Code treats an instruction-governed legacy route tombstone as resolved without restoring canonical domain ownership.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The deleted forbidden route must not be added back to canonical domain paths.

requirements.requirement: The exact implementation head passes TypeScript and production build with the extended execution-route evidence contract.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The correction must not introduce type or production build regressions.
